title: Stay Fair! Ensuring Group Fairness in Diffusion Models Across Guidance Scales

paper.title: Stay Fair ! Ensuring Group Fairness in Diffusion Models Across Guidance Scales
paper.abstract:
Abstract Diffusion models steer conditional generation with a tunable guidance scale
to trade off prompt alignment and diversity.
However, existing debiasing techniques are optimized for a single scale, degrading fairness when users adjust this parameter.
We trace this behavior to a previously overlooked source by decomposing total bias into two components: a model bias and a guidance bias. While prior work primarily targets the former, we show that the guidance bias grows monotonically with the guidance scale, eventually dominating the high-guidance regimes users prefer.
To address this, we extend Strong Demographic Parity to guidance and derive a condition under which the target distribution retains its group ratio across guidance scales.
We propose StayFair, which leverages this condition to design fair guidance algorithms in both regimes.
For classifier guidance, it equalizes the classifier’s output distributions across groups; for classifier-free guidance, it shifts the null embedding by a prompt-dependent offset.
Because StayFair modifies only the guidance step,
it is orthogonal to model debiasing and can be layered onto existing fair diffusion models to extend their fairness across guidance scales.
Across class-conditional and text-to-image generation, StayFair decouples fairness from the guidance scale without sacrificing image quality. 1 1 1 Code: https://github.com/Kim-Myeong-Soo/stay-fair

sections.heading: 1 Introduction
sections.text: Recent advances in diffusion models have enabled high-quality conditional generation, particularly in text-to-image synthesis [ 1 , 2 ] . Guidance is central to the widespread adoption of conditional diffusion models by controlling how conditioning information influences generation [ 3 , 4 ] . However, diffusion models often exhibit biases related to sensitive attributes such as gender, race, and age [ 5 , 6 ] , and may amplify biases present in the training data [ 7 ] . Prior work on group fairness in diffusion models has largely aimed to align the generated group distribution with a desired target. One line of research consists of attribute-based methods , which explicitly condition generation on sensitive attributes or steer samples toward target group ratios at inference time [ 8 , 9 ] . These methods directly control the generated group distribution, rather than reducing bias in the underlying diffusion model. Another line of work applies train-time debiasing directly to the diffusion model, targeting its learned distribution. Representative approaches include text encoder finetuning and concept editing [ 10 , 11 ] . These methods typically rely on guidance with a fixed guidance scale during validation and generation to ensure reliable attribute separation. However, the behavior of existing fairness methods under varying guidance scales remains underexplored. Users adjust the guidance scale according to their generation objectives, for example to trade off condition alignment, image quality, and diversity. Prior work typically considers fairness only at a fixed guidance scale, implicitly assuming that it generalizes across scales. As shown in Figure 1 , fairness often fails once the guidance scale changes. This is because prior methods primarily target the model distribution, whereas guidance affects fairness through a distinct mechanism. Motivated by this observation, we define guidance scale-invariant group fairness as an extension of group-fair generation beyond a fixed guidance scale. We propose a framework to decompose original bias into two distinct sources: a static model bias and a scale-dependent guidance bias . Unlike prior work that primarily targets model bias at a fixed scale, our objective is to achieve fair guidance by reducing this dynamic bias across scales. To provide a rigorous foundation, we extend Strong Demographic Parity (SDP) [ 12 ] to guidance, identifying a condition under which the target distribution remains fair across guidance scales. Inspired by this fairness principle, we introduce StayFair, which addresses guidance bias in both major guidance regimes: for classifier guidance (CG) [ 3 ] , it enforces the proposed condition through a debiased classifier with group-fairness constraints, while for classifier-free guidance (CFG) [ 4 ] , it utilizes an adaptive null prompt to rebalance bias without sacrificing prompt alignment. Our experiments show that StayFair preserves fairness across guidance scales in both CG and CFG. On class-conditional generation with CG, evaluated on CelebA [ 13 ] with ADM [ 3 ] , StayFair reduces guidance-scale sensitivity in the generated group ratio while maintaining competitive image quality. On text-to-image generation with CFG, evaluated on occupation prompts [ 6 ] using SD1.5 [ 1 ] and SD3 [ 2 ] , StayFair remains effective for vanilla diffusion models. The same holds when it is layered on top of debiased models such as FT [ 10 ] and UCE [ 11 ] , showing that guidance bias is distinct from model bias and requires separate correction. Additional analyses use our bias decomposition framework to make bias amplification more interpretable, examining why amplification can be asymmetric across groups and why its direction can vary across prompts. Figure 1 : StayFair preserves group fairness as users vary the guidance scale. Users choose the guidance scale to control how strongly generation follows the prompt. Thus, group fairness should remain stable regardless of users’ scale choice. However, prior work [ 4 , 10 ] typically optimizes or evaluates fairness at a fixed scale, failing to maintain group fairness under different user selected scales. StayFair mitigates guidance-induced bias, enabling guidance scale-invariant group fairness .

sections.heading: 2 Related Work
sections.text: Bias and fairness in diffusion models. The growing deployment of diffusion models in real-world applications [ 1 , 2 ] has intensified concerns about their biased distributions over sensitive attributes such as gender, race, age, and culture [ 5 , 14 , 15 , 7 ] . These biases have been shown to be amplified beyond the training distribution [ 6 , 16 , 17 , 18 ] , yet their underlying mechanisms remain poorly understood. To reduce these biases, one approach is the attribute-based method , which injects the conditioning attribute through guidance [ 8 , 19 ] , prompt embeddings [ 20 ] , or latent manipulation [ 21 ] . However, these methods control the sampled attribute distribution without directly debiasing the underlying model distribution. Another line of work consists of train-time methods , which take two forms: fine-tuning the model with fairness-aware objectives [ 10 , 22 , 23 ] ; and updating specific modules such as text embeddings [ 24 , 25 ] or cross-attention layers [ 11 ] . These methods focus on debiasing the model distribution at a fixed guidance scale. StayFair debiases guidance, a distinct source of bias that grows with guidance scale, and is orthogonal to debiasing methods. Guidance in diffusion models. Guidance is the standard mechanism for controlling conditional diffusion generation: it improves image quality and condition alignment while reducing diversity [ 1 , 2 ] . Common variants include classifier guidance (CG) [ 3 , 28 , 29 ] , classifier-free guidance (CFG) [ 4 , 30 , 31 ] , and autoguidance (AG) [ 32 , 33 , 34 ] , differing in how the conditioning signal is constructed. Recent work [ 9 , 35 ] reports that varying the guidance scale also shifts demographic composition, exposing a fairness dimension to this tradeoff. However, no prior method directly reduces guidance bias amplification. To address this gap, we propose StayFair, a guidance debiasing method that preserves fairness across user-controlled guidance scales. Group fairness for classifiers. Group fairness has been widely studied in computer vision [ 36 , 37 , 38 ] . Generally, it requires that some statistic of the predictor be matched across sensitive groups [ 39 ] . Common criteria such as demographic parity [ 39 ] and equalized odds [ 40 ] are defined through group-wise averages of predictions. These criteria are typically achieved through constrained classification [ 41 , 42 ] or group-distributionally robust training [ 43 , 44 ] . A stronger notion, Strong Demographic Parity (SDP) [ 12 ] , requires prediction distributions to match across groups. Prior work enforces SDP by minimizing discrepancies between group-conditional distributions, using Wasserstein distance [ 45 ] , total variation [ 46 ] , or optimal-transport objectives [ 47 ] . Building on this distributional view of fairness, we characterize the classifier fairness required to preserve group proportions under guidance and extend SDP to guidance functions.

sections.heading: 3.3 The overlooked impact of guidance bias
sections.text: We reveal the overlooked consequences of Bias G w \mathrm{Bias}_{\mathrm{G}}^{w} through two scenarios where its impact is most critical: its emergence in vanilla models and persistence in debiased models ( Figure 1 ). First, in vanilla models, while guidance is known to amplify the majority attribute, we further analyze its mechanism as a process of extrapolation from the unconditional model ( Section 5.3 ). We find that minor skews in this baseline are magnified into distinct bias trends as the guidance scale increases, suggesting that guidance bias should be treated as a distinct phenomenon from model bias. Second, even models debiased for a specific setting remain vulnerable; as the guidance scale w w deviates from the reference scale w ref w_{\mathrm{ref}} , the lack of scale-awareness causes the group distribution to drift away from the target, leading to a collapse of fairness ( Section A.2 ). Together, these observations indicate that guidance scale-invariant group fairness cannot be achieved by model debiasing alone; it requires a direct intervention on the guidance mechanism itself.

sections.heading: 4 StayFair: Fair Diffusion Across Guidance Scales
sections.text: Building on these observations, we develop a framework to reduce guidance bias by identifying when guidance remains fair across scales. We first derive a sufficient condition for such fairness ( Section 4.1 ). We then propose StayFair, which leverages this condition to design fair guidance algorithms in both CG and CFG regimes ( Section 4.2 ).

sections.heading: 6 Conclusion
sections.text: We propose StayFair, a framework that decomposes total bias to expose its overlooked guidance component across CG and CFG. We demonstrate that guidance is a key driver of bias amplification in T2I diffusion models, and that StayFair mitigates this effect, preserves fairness across guidance scales, and composes naturally with existing models. Limitations. We focus on binary gender stereotypes to study guidance scale-invariant fairness in a clearly scoped setting, while validating the phenomenon across diverse modalities and guidance types. Extending to multi-attribute and intersectional biases is a promising direction for future work. Broader impact. By highlighting guidance bias as an overlooked source of unfairness, our work encourages future research on debiasing guidance beyond the model distribution. We hope this perspective promotes fairness studies under more realistic generation scenarios, where guidance scales are routinely adjusted by users or downstream pipelines.

sections.heading: C.1 Class-conditional generation
sections.text: Training. We build our sampling pipeline on the official ADM-G codebase [ 3 ] and train the classifier on the CelebA dataset with images resized to 64 × 64 64\times 64 resolution, using the Male attribute as the confounder. The diffusion process consists of 1000 1000 steps with a cosine noise schedule, and learned sigmas are rescaled during training. We train all models using the Adam optimizer with a learning rate of 3 × 10 − 4 3\times 10^{-4} and weight decay 1 × 10 − 2 1\times 10^{-2} , for a total of 800 800 k iterations with batch size 128 128 . The learning rate is annealed during training. All experiments are conducted on 2x NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4090 GPUs. StayFair settings. StayFair follows the baseline CG training framework, introducing an additional constraint term in the optimization objective after the first 5 % 5\% of training while keeping all other settings unchanged. We set λ = 3 \lambda=3 in Eq. 8 of the main paper, selected from { 1 , 3 , 5 } \{1,3,5\} . We approximate it by sampling t t from a random window of width 50 50 in each batch, where the window center is itself P2 weight [ 66 ] sampled. We additionally apply group-aware resampling to mitigate training imbalance across sensitive groups. Since the Wasserstein distance is computed in 2D (probability and timestep), we define the cost as the original distance plus a 0.2-weighted penalty for the logSNR(Signal-to-Noise Ratio) discrepancy between corresponding time indices. Baselines. We apply RW [ 44 ] and GDRO [ 43 ] to the noisy classifier f ϕ ​ ( x t , t ) f_{\phi}(x_{t},t) used for CG. RW is implemented by reweighting samples so that groups are sampled with equal probability. For GDRO, we average the classifier loss over sampled timesteps within each group and apply the standard group-DRO update to the resulting group losses.

sections.heading: C.2 Text-to-image generation
sections.text: Common settings. For experiments with SD1.5 and SD3, images are generated using different sampling schedulers and guidance scales. SD1.5 uses the DPMSolver multistep scheduler with 30 denoising steps, while SD3 employs the FlowMatchEulerDiscreteScheduler with 28 steps. Image resolution is set to 512 × 512 512\times 512 for both models. For SD1.5, we evaluate guidance scales w ∈ { 2.5 , 5.0 , 7.5 , 10.0 , 12.5 } w\in\{2.5,5.0,7.5,10.0,12.5\} and generate 100 images for each occupation × \times guidance scale combination. For SD3, we evaluate guidance scales w ∈ { 1.5 , 3.0 , 4.5 , 6.0 , 7.5 } w\in\{1.5,3.0,4.5,6.0,7.5\} . All experiments are conducted on 1 × 1\times NVIDIA A100 (80 GB) GPU. Occupations and prompts. Following [ 6 ] , we use 33 occupations and five prompt templates in evaluation. Table 5 lists occupations and Table 6 lists templates used in our experiments. sections.heading: C.3 Baseline implementations
sections.text: Fine-Tuning Diffusion (FT). We use the pre-trained checkpoint released by the authors. FTDiff provides several checkpoints corresponding to different trained components of Stable Diffusion, including prefix tuning and LoRA fine-tuning. As many existing methods also consider fine-tuning the text encoder, we adopt the checkpoint “finetune-text-encoder 09190215checkpoint-9800_exportedtext_encoder_lora_EMA.pth”. Unified Concept Editing (UCE). Following the official GitHub repository, we train UCE from scratch. Since UCE requires a predefined set of professions for training, we adopt the same 33-profession configuration as in our list for fair comparison with the other baselines. Fair Diffusion (FD). We use [“female person”, “male person”] as the editing prompts. The guidance direction (addition or subtraction) is randomly selected between the two concepts. The editing guidance scale is set to 4. The threshold, momentum scale, and momentum beta are set to 0.9, 0.5, and 0.6, respectively. Both concepts are assigned equal weights of 1. Weak Guidance (WG). Since the official code is not publicly available, we implement the method following the description in the original paper. We confirm that our implementation reproduces the reported performance on the ten occupations considered in the paper. During generation, the modified conditioning incorporating the attribute direction is used exclusively for the first 10% of the denoising steps. For the remaining steps, the modified conditioning and the original conditioning are alternated. Perturbation Attention Guidance (PAG). For the PAG baseline, we use the publicly released StableDiffusionPAGPipeline from hyoungwoncho/sd_perturbed_attention_guidance on Hugging Face. We set the perturbed layer to the first self-attention layer in the U-Net mid-block ( m0 ) and sweep the PAG scale over { 1 , 2 , 3 , 4 } \{1,2,3,4\} without CFG.

Ensuring Group Fairness in Diffusion Models Across Guidance Scales Myeongsoo Kim Affiliation: POSTECH Eunji Kim † † thanks: The work was done prior to joining Amazon. Affiliation: Amazon Minwoo Chae Affiliation: POSTECH Sangwoo Mo Affiliation: POSTECH Abstract Diffusion models steer conditional generation with a tunable guidance scale to trade off prompt alignment and diversity. However, existing debiasing techniques are optimized for a single scale, degrading fairness when users adjust this parameter. We trace this behavior to a previously overlooked source by decomposing total bias into two components: a model bias and a guidance bias. While prior work primarily targets the former, we show that the guidance bias grows monotonically with the guidance scale, eventually dominating the high-guidance regimes users prefer. To address this, we extend Strong Demographic Parity to guidance and derive a condition under which the target distribution retains its group ratio across guidance scales. We propose StayFair, which leverages this condition to design fair guidance algorithms in both regimes. For classifier guidance, it equalizes the classifier’s output distributions across groups; for classifier-free guidance, it shifts the null embedding by a prompt-dependent offset. Because StayFair modifies only the guidance step, it is orthogonal to model debiasing and can be layered onto existing fair diffusion models to extend their fairness across guidance scales. Across class-conditional and text-to-image generation, StayFair decouples fairness from the guidance scale without sacrificing image quality. 1 1 1 Code: https://github.com/Kim-Myeong-Soo/stay-fair 1 Introduction Recent advances in diffusion models have enabled high-quality conditional generation, particularly in text-to-image synthesis [ 1 , 2 ] . Guidance is central to the widespread adoption of conditional diffusion models by controlling how conditioning information influences generation [ 3 , 4 ] . However, diffusion models often exhibit biases related to sensitive attributes such as gender, race, and age [ 5 , 6 ] , and may amplify biases present in the training data [ 7 ] . Prior work on group fairness in diffusion models has largely aimed to align the generated group distribution with a desired target. One line of research consists of attribute-based methods , which explicitly condition generation on sensitive attributes or steer samples toward target group ratios at inference time [ 8 , 9 ] . These methods directly control the generated group distribution, rather than reducing bias in the underlying diffusion model. Another line of work applies train-time debiasing directly to the diffusion model, targeting its learned distribution. Representative approaches include text encoder finetuning and concept editing [ 10 , 11 ] . These methods typically rely on guidance with a fixed guidance scale during validation and generation to ensure reliable attribute separation. However, the behavior of existing fairness methods under varying guidance scales remains underexplored. Users adjust the guidance scale according to their generation objectives, for example to trade off condition alignment, image quality, and diversity. Prior work typically considers fairness only at a fixed guidance scale, implicitly assuming that it generalizes across scales. As shown in Figure 1 , fairness often fails once the guidance scale changes. This is because prior methods primarily target the model distribution, whereas guidance affects fairness through a distinct mechanism. Motivated by this observation, we define guidance scale-invariant group fairness as an extension of group-fair generation beyond a fixed guidance scale. We propose a framework to decompose original bias into two distinct sources: a static model bias and a scale-dependent guidance bias . Unlike prior work that primarily targets model bias at a fixed scale, our objective is to achieve fair guidance by reducing this dynamic bias across scales. To provide a rigorous foundation, we extend Strong Demographic Parity (SDP) [ 12 ] to guidance, identifying a condition under which the target distribution remains fair across guidance scales. Inspired by this fairness principle, we introduce StayFair, which addresses guidance bias in both major guidance regimes: for classifier guidance (CG) [ 3 ] , it enforces the proposed condition through a debiased classifier with group-fairness constraints, while for classifier-free guidance (CFG) [ 4 ] , it utilizes an adaptive null prompt to rebalance bias without sacrificing prompt alignment. Our experiments show that StayFair preserves fairness across guidance scales in both CG and CFG. On class-conditional generation with CG, evaluated on CelebA [ 13 ] with ADM [ 3 ] , StayFair reduces guidance-scale sensitivity in the generated group ratio while maintaining competitive image quality. On text-to-image generation with CFG, evaluated on occupation prompts [ 6 ] using SD1.5 [ 1 ] and SD3 [ 2 ] , StayFair remains effective for vanilla diffusion models. The same holds when it is layered on top of debiased models such as FT [ 10 ] and UCE [ 11 ] , showing that guidance bias is distinct from model bias and requires separate correction. Additional analyses use our bias decomposition framework to make bias amplification more interpretable, examining why amplification can be asymmetric across groups and why its direction can vary across prompts. Figure 1 : StayFair preserves group fairness as users vary the guidance scale. Users choose the guidance scale to control how strongly generation follows the prompt. Thus, group fairness should remain stable regardless of users’ scale choice. However, prior work [ 4 , 10 ] typically optimizes or evaluates fairness at a fixed scale, failing to maintain group fairness under different user selected scales. StayFair mitigates guidance-induced bias, enabling guidance scale-invariant group fairness . 2 Related Work Bias and fairness in diffusion models. The growing deployment of diffusion models in real-world applications [ 1 , 2 ] has intensified concerns about their biased distributions over sensitive attributes such as gender, race, age, and culture [ 5 , 14 , 15 , 7 ] . These biases have been shown to be amplified beyond the training distribution [ 6 , 16 , 17 , 18 ] , yet their underlying mechanisms remain poorly understood. To reduce these biases, one approach is the attribute-based method , which injects the conditioning attribute through guidance [ 8 , 19 ] , prompt embeddings [ 20 ] , or latent manipulation [ 21 ] . However, these methods control the sampled attribute distribution without directly debiasing the underlying model distribution. Another line of work consists of train-time methods , which take two forms: fine-tuning the model with fairness-aware objectives [ 10 , 22 , 23 ] ; and updating specific modules such as text embeddings [ 24 , 25 ] or cross-attention layers [ 11 ] . These methods focus on debiasing the model distribution at a fixed guidance scale. StayFair debiases guidance, a distinct source of bias that grows with guidance scale, and is orthogonal to debiasing methods. Guidance in diffusion models. Guidance is the standard mechanism for controlling conditional diffusion generation: it improves image quality and condition alignment while reducing diversity [ 1 , 2 ] . Common variants include classifier guidance (CG) [ 3 , 28 , 29 ] , classifier-free guidance (CFG) [ 4 , 30 , 31 ] , and autoguidance (AG) [ 32 , 33 , 34 ] , differing in how the conditioning signal is constructed. Recent work [ 9 , 35 ] reports that varying the guidance scale also shifts demographic composition, exposing a fairness dimension to this tradeoff. However, no prior method directly reduces guidance bias amplification. To address this gap, we propose StayFair, a guidance debiasing method that preserves fairness across user-controlled guidance scales. Group fairness for classifiers. Group fairness has been widely studied in computer vision [ 36 , 37 , 38 ] . Generally, it requires that some statistic of the predictor be matched across sensitive groups [ 39 ] . Common criteria such as demographic parity [ 39 ] and equalized odds [ 40 ] are defined through group-wise averages of predictions. These criteria are typically achieved through constrained classification [ 41 , 42 ] or group-distributionally robust training [ 43 , 44 ] . A stronger notion, Strong Demographic Parity (SDP) [ 12 ] , requires prediction distributions to match across groups. Prior work enforces SDP by minimizing discrepancies between group-conditional distributions, using Wasserstein distance [ 45 ] , total variation [ 46 ] , or optimal-transport objectives [ 47 ] . Building on this distributional view of fairness, we characterize the classifier fairness required to preserve group proportions under guidance and extend SDP to guidance functions. 3 Bias from Diffusion Guidance 3.1 Preliminary: diffusion models and guidance Diffusion models [ 48 , 49 ] generate clean data X 0 ∼ p 0 ​ ( x ) X_{0}\sim p_{0}(x) by reversing a forward corruption process { X t } \{X_{t}\} that progressively perturbs X 0 X_{0} with Gaussian noise. We demonstrate that guidance is a key driver of bias amplification in T2I diffusion models, and that StayFair mitigates this effect, preserves fairness across guidance scales, and composes naturally with existing models. Limitations. We focus on binary gender stereotypes to study guidance scale-invariant fairness in a clearly scoped setting, while validating the phenomenon across diverse modalities and guidance types. Extending to multi-attribute and intersectional biases is a promising direction for future work. Broader impact. By highlighting guidance bias as an overlooked source of unfairness, our work encourages future research on debiasing guidance beyond the model distribution. We hope this perspective promotes fairness studies under more realistic generation scenarios, where guidance scales are routinely adjusted by users or downstream pipelines.
